<STRUCT_0001>
This section is the analogue of Section <REF_0001>
for ringed topoi.
In the following few sections we will use the following notions:
<STRUCT_0002>
<STRUCT_0003> A sheaf of ideals <MATH_0001> on
a ringed topos <MATH_0002> is <TEXTITOPEN_0001>locally nilpotent<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>
if any local section of <MATH_0003> is locally nilpotent.
<STRUCT_0004> A <TEXTITOPEN_0002>thickening<TEXTITCLOSE_0002> of ringed topoi is a morphism
<MATH_0004>
of ringed topoi such that
<STRUCT_0005>
<STRUCT_0006> <MATH_0005> is an equivalence <MATH_0006>,
<STRUCT_0007> the map <MATH_0007>
is surjective, and
<STRUCT_0008> the kernel of <MATH_0008> is a locally nilpotent sheaf of ideals.
<STRUCT_0009>
<STRUCT_0010> A <TEXTITOPEN_0003>first order thickening<TEXTITCLOSE_0003> of ringed topoi is a thickening
<MATH_0009>
of ringed topoi such that <MATH_0010> has square zero.
<STRUCT_0011> It is clear how to define
<TEXTITOPEN_0004>morphisms of thickenings of ringed topoi<TEXTITCLOSE_0004>,
<TEXTITOPEN_0005>morphisms of thickenings of ringed topoi over a base ringed topos<TEXTITCLOSE_0005>, etc.

If

We obtain a short exact sequence

Modules on Sites, Lemma <REF_0002>
